key_insight: A generalized, label-free safety measure can be learned from large-scale naturalistic driving data to proactively predict collision risk, providing real-time warnings that secure extra reaction time before crashes and near-crashes.
problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity and cost of labeled crash data and the lack of scalable, generalizable real-time risk metrics for autonomous driving systems.
method: Self-supervised training on large-scale naturalistic driving data to learn a generalized collision-risk score without explicit crash labels.
Temporal prediction of near-future risk using vehicle trajectories and scene context to trigger real-time warnings for crashes and near-crashes.
Large-scale validation showing the learned measure accurately anticipates incidents and increases available reaction time for interventions.
impact: Enables ML and AV teams to build scalable, label-efficient safety predictors and early-warning systems, improving validation and operational safety without relying on rare labeled crash events.
visual_elements: Scene overlay: driving camera / bird's-eye view with a color-coded risk heatmap around the ego vehicle to show where risk is detected.
Timeline chart: risk-score trace aligned with a crash/near-crash event showing lead time gained by the model versus baselines.
Performance plot: precision–recall or early-warning ROC comparing the learned risk measure to conventional heuristics.
Icon panel: dataset scale (fleet icon), label-free/self-supervised learning, real-time warning (alarm), and increased reaction time (clock)
paper_title: Learning collision risk proactively from naturalistic driving data at scale
paper_authors: Yiru Jiao, Simeon C. Calvert, Sander van Cranenburgh, Hans van Lint
